subject: estonian
summary: Estonian cards are tidy: text renders correctly (õ, ä, ö, ü), the questions are complete, and each attached reading text is the correct article with no other questions on the page. The essay card is well done, with the four official criteria, their weightings and a score picker for each. The weaker cards are the 30-mark commentary, whose whole scheme is one comma-joined list of topic words with no criteria or marks, and a 5-mark question whose scheme is one 35-line paragraph on a phone worth all 5 marks at once. The grey English language-rule note is attached to every scheme, and the term to be explained in vocabulary cards runs onto the instruction.

issues.title: 30-mark commentary scheme is a bare keyword list
issues.detail: Card 1's scheme is a single tick box reading 'Rahumeelsed meeleavaldused ja vägivaldsed väljaastumised, kodanikuosalus, sõnavabadus, vabatahtlik töö, noorte panus, ... jne.' with no explanation that these are possible themes, no criteria and no marks. The essay card for the same paper family (card 4) shows that the scheme applies four weighted criteria to tasks II and III, but they are not shown here.
issues.suggested_fix: Label the list 'Possible themes' as bullets and show the same four criteria with weightings used on card 4, scaled to 30 marks.

issues.title: One long paragraph worth all 5 marks
issues.detail: Card 2's scheme is a single sample answer of about 35 lines on the phone (16 on desktop) with one 5m badge, under 'Select the points you actually got'. A student cannot claim part marks, and the footer strip truncates it mid-word.
issues.suggested_fix: Break into the separate arguments (CO2 share, natural processes, solar activity, anticyclones, ice-age comparison) as short rows; label as sample answer.

issues.title: Grey language-rule note in every scheme
issues.detail: 'The examination requires every answer in ESTONIAN. The paper prints the rule on page 2: "..."' appears in each card, sometimes with extra commentary ('The scheme heads them: “Võimalikud vastused:”.', 'The scheme prints: “II ja III ülesande hindamisel ...:”.'). Under the 1-mark answer on card 3 it is four lines against the answer's two.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove; where the scheme heading matters show it as a plain label ('Possible answers').

issues.title: Term or title run onto the instruction
issues.detail: Card 3: '...järgmised sõnad ja väljendid: ebausk' (plural instruction, one word, no emphasis). Card 4: 'Vali üks antud teemadest. Rikkaim on see, kes on rahul vähesega. (Sokrates)' reads as three sentences in a row with the title not set off. Card 1 keeps the paper's '/---/' omission mark inside the quotation, which looks like a glitch out of context.
issues.suggested_fix: Put the term/title on its own line in bold or quotes; replace '/---/' with '[...]'.

issues.title: No marks on multi-point scheme
issues.detail: Card 5 has three possible answers of very uneven length (13 lines, 4 lines, 5 lines on the phone) with no marks and no statement of how many are needed for 5 marks.
issues.suggested_fix: State how the 5 marks are awarded; shorten the first point to its key idea.

good_examples.why: Essay scheme with four weighted criteria and per-criterion score pickers; compact on desktop.
One-line vocabulary answer with the right text attached.
Three distinct possible answers, clearly separated.
